claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation a bit better.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending sixth form, college, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is in sixth form doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in sixth form doing his A-levels, I need to check a few more details to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex working at all? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work. He's just focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not actually sure about that - I don't know if he receives any benefits in his own name.

## Assessment Result

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Here's the situation:**

✓ **Positive factors:**
- Alex is 18 and in approved education (sixth form, doing A-levels)
- He lives with you in the UK
- He's not working 24 hours or more per week
- He's under 20 years old

**However:**
- You're unsure whether Alex receives any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)

This is important because according to the rules, you would stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts getting certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit.

**My recommendation:** If Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own name, you would likely be eligible for Child Benefit. I'd suggest checking with Alex or reviewing any correspondence you may have received to confirm whether he claims any benefits. If he doesn't, you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him while he continues his A-levels.
